_note: GAM Research forecast drivers for Sumitomo Chemical India (consolidated, ₹ crore). One reportable segment (crop protection, plus environmental-health and animal-nutrition distribution). Revenue grows at a single rate; EBITDA margin is a driver; treasury income = yield × opening cash, deposits and investments. Valued on P/E, as the street does.
_revenueWhy: FY27: H1 −1% (worst kharif monsoon since 2015, parent's Japan orders halved); H2 +3% on a weak rabi (El Niño, low reservoirs) offset by the restart of animal-nutrition sales lost in Q3FY26. FY28-29: a normal monsoon, Japan exports normalising, new plants for the parent (Bhavnagar Q4FY27, Tarapur/Dahej FY28-29) and 1-2 launches a year. Still below the street's ~20% for FY28: revenue has not grown since FY23.
_marginWhy: 20.7% in FY26; 21.3% in H1FY27 but H2 is seasonally weaker (18.6% in H2FY26). Management aims to stay at or above 20%; CRISIL expects 19-20%. Animal-nutrition pass-through sales (4-5% margin) dilute the percentage.
_capexWhy: Maintenance ₹50-70 cr a year plus the ₹55 cr Bhavnagar plant (FY27), ₹150 cr Dahej herbicide intermediate and ₹20 cr Tarapur fitments (FY28-29), all for the parent. CRISIL: ₹150-160 cr a year over the medium term.
_depWhy: FY26 depreciation ₹66 cr ≈ 7.4% of average gross block.
_treasuryWhy: Applied to opening cash, deposits and investments (₹2,113 cr at Mar-26, company figure): FY26 other income ₹147 cr on ₹1,668 cr opening = 8.8%, because cash builds through the year. H1FY27 ₹91 cr excluding the insurance claim. Lower from FY28 as deposit rates fall.
_otherIncomeWhy: FY27: ₹26.9 cr business-interruption insurance claim for the FY23 Bhavnagar fire (Q1FY27; Screener shows it in other income).

otherTreasury._why: Corporate deposits, bank deposits and non-current financial investments reported under other assets: the company's cash and liquid investments were ₹2,113 cr at Mar-26 vs ₹1,274 cr of cash and investments on Screener.

_taxWhy: FY26 effective 26%; new regime ~25.2% plus disallowances.

dcf._betaWhy: Debt-free with a large cash pile, but earnings swing with the monsoon: slightly below market sensitivity.
dcf._tgWhy: Indian crop-protection demand grows with farm output and prices; 6% nominal.
dcf._fadeGrowthWhy: Industry growth of 5-6% plus share gains from the parent's new molecules.
dcf._fadeCapexWhy: Asset-light formulator; capex rises only for plants built for the parent.

bull.label: Bull
bull.narrative: Normal monsoons from FY28; the parent's new molecules and plants built for it lift growth to the mid-teens; Japan orders recover; margin ~21.5%.

bear.label: Bear
bear.narrative: Another weak monsoon or a glyphosate restriction; Chinese generic prices fall; growth stays in low single digits; margin ~19%.

methods.name: P/E
methods.why: How the street values Sumitomo (ICICI Direct 45x, Anand Rathi 40x, ICICI Securities 36.5x, all on FY28E EPS). 28x = its ~42x one-year-forward median since 2023, cut by the ~23% sector de-rating (PI Industries, Dhanuka) to ~32x, and again for growth: the street's multiples come with 13-21% a year EPS growth; we forecast ~8%.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.why: Values the business and the cash separately. A P/E on total earnings capitalises interest income at 28x, i.e. pays ~1.6 rupees for each rupee of cash. 18x ≈ the ~34x median since listing less the same de-rating and growth discount (ICICI Securities used 29x).

methods.name: DCF
methods.why: Tests whether cash flows support the price: 15-year FCFF, Ke 11.6%, terminal growth 6%, plus net cash.
